---
title: "pyEllipse"
subtitle: "Hotelling's T-squared statistic and confidence ellipses for multivariate data"
---

pyEllipse computes Hotelling's T-squared statistic, its control limits, and the
confidence ellipses and ellipsoids drawn from them, for outlier detection and score
plots of PCA, PLS and other multivariate models. Its Hotelling functions are the Python
counterpart of the [HotellingEllipse](https://github.com/ChristianGoueguel/HotellingEllipse)
R package and give the same results (see [Validation](#validation)).

| Function | Purpose |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| [`hotelling_parameters`](reference/hotelling_parameters.qmd) | T-squared of each observation, cutoffs, and the semi-axes and rotation of the ellipse |
| [`hotelling_coordinates`](reference/hotelling_coordinates.qmd) | Points of the T-squared ellipse (2D) or ellipsoid (3D), for plotting |
| [`confidence_ellipse`](reference/confidence_ellipse.qmd) | Confidence ellipses and ellipsoids of raw data, optionally by group and with robust estimates |

The [Theory](theory.qmd) page gives the formulas behind each function and states when
each limit is exact.

## Installation

```bash
pip install pyEllipse
```

## Quick start

Compute T-squared on the first two principal components of the wine data, and flag the
samples above the 99% limit:

```{python}
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import load_wine
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from pyEllipse import hotelling_coordinates, hotelling_parameters

X = StandardScaler().fit_transform(load_wine().data)
scores = PCA().fit_transform(X)

res = hotelling_parameters(scores, pcx=1, pcy=2, method="beta")
t2 = res["Tsquared"]["value"]
print(f"99% limit: {res['cutoff_99pct']:.2f}")
print("Samples above it:", np.flatnonzero(t2 > res["cutoff_99pct"]).tolist())
```

`hotelling_coordinates(scores, pcx=1, pcy=2, conf_limit=0.99, method="beta")` returns the
points of the matching ellipse, for plotting. The
[PCA example](examples/pca-outliers.qmd) goes through a complete analysis.

::: {.callout-important}
## T-squared values changed in version 0.2.0

Up to version 0.1.5, `hotelling_parameters` returned T-squared scaled by
$(n-k)/(k(n-1))$, while the cutoffs were not, so comparing the two missed outliers.
From version 0.2.0, `Tsquared` is on the same scale as the cutoffs. See the
[changelog](https://github.com/ChristianGoueguel/pyEllipse/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
:::

## Validation {#validation}

The [test suite](https://github.com/ChristianGoueguel/pyEllipse/tree/main/tests) runs on
every change, on Python 3.9 to 3.14. For `hotelling_parameters` and
`hotelling_coordinates`, it checks the formulas of the [Theory](theory.qmd) page
directly (T-squared against the squared Mahalanobis distance, the ellipse points against
the limit, the semi-axes and rotation against the ellipse points), checks that about 5%
of simulated observations exceed the 95% Beta limit, and compares both functions with
the HotellingEllipse 1.3.0 R package on a reference data set, to within a relative
$10^{-10}$. The examples in the [reference](reference/index.qmd) pages are run as tests
too; for `confidence_ellipse`, this example is so far the only test.
